name: GARDENS CABIN
detail: I made a reservation for my last day of travel. The reviews were good, and I chose a cabin because I didn’t want to deal with finding a place for my large suitcase for a week. I opted for breakfast since drinks are available but food isn’t. The menu had fewer options than I expected. It was great that there were soup curry and fish typical of Sapporo. I was looking forward to enjoying the large public bath, but the water was lukewarm, which was disappointing since I wanted a hot bath. I think it’s nice to go early as it was less crowded then. The cabin had accordion curtains, and it was nice to watch TV with headphones available for loan. However, I was bothered by the noise from the cheaper lodging in the vertical hole; it was so disruptive that I felt like it was almost all night. I thought they might as well have booked a regular hotel if they were going to be that noisy, and I fell asleep thinking about that. In the morning, I woke up around 5:00 and it was a good decision to start my day early, allowing me to wash my face leisurely. I could take my time doing my makeup after returning to the cabin, and it was great that I could focus on washing my face and brushing my teeth in peace. A few hours later, it was all packed, and the young guests were getting ready properly, but I noticed that even when the hairdryer’s cord was in the sink, they just left it as is. The outlets were built-in, but since it’s near water, it seemed dangerous. I thought it would be reassuring if the staff checked regularly. Since it’s a capsule hotel, it’s unavoidable, but my impression was that there were quite a few people without manners. The staff, especially the males, seemed more polite. I had too high expectations due to the overly positive comments, so next time, I’ll book a cabin without breakfast. It’s perfect just to stay and store my suitcase! On the way back, I walked through the underground for about 15 minutes and came out near Sapporo Station. It was convenient to go underground from the building right next to it!

name: Hotel Plus Hostel SAPPORO
detail: 1️⃣ Convenient transportation. It's just a 2-minute walk to the bus station for New Chitose Airport; a 6-minute walk to the Namboku Line Odori Station. 2️⃣ Convenient shopping. Various stores like Daikoku Drugstore, Don Quijote, capsule toy shops, and Soup Curry SAMA are right downstairs. 3️⃣ The water pressure in the shower is strong and warm, not cold at all. 4️⃣ The front desk provides breakfast coupons, and the service is very friendly. 5️⃣ Good soundproofing. Stayed for 6 nights and barely heard any noise, sleep was comfortable.

name: The Centurion Sauna Rest & Stay Sapporo Male Only
detail: Rating: ★★★★☆ Purpose of use: Short trip Room type: Standard Cabin Upper level This was my first time using this service, and the check-in process to the guest room was very smooth. The polite response from the staff, including the female staff member at the reception, was impressive, and I was able to spend my time comfortably until checkout. The cabin was clean, and the large public bath was comfortable with a good range of amenities. I felt that the variety of baths was limited, with the sauna being the main feature. The dining options available on the food floor are plentiful. It’s good for those who have eaten well in the Sapporo and Susukino area to enjoy a drink, or for guests to indulge in food and drink at the hotel. However, the shared toilet on the cabin floor had a slight odor, and the cleaning of the cabins started earlier than checkout time at 10 AM, which is a downside. Nevertheless, I would like to use this service again if I have the opportunity to experience a break from the ordinary.

name: Hotel Abest Sapporo
detail: The location is very satisfying as it is close to Susukino Station and you can catch the airport limousine bus right across the street. There is enough floor space for two people to spread out their suitcases. The bed is comfortable and clean. The staff are all friendly (many of them speak English well). The breakfast is decent, so if you have time, it would be nice to have a meal there for a day (but I wouldn't recommend it if there's something specific you want to eat and can't miss a meal).

name: Hotel Grand Terrace Chitose
detail: It is close to Chitose Airport, and for those without a rental car, they also provide transportation to the airport. My husband and I used this hotel the day before we returned to our hometown. The price was reasonably low, and the room was quite spacious. There is also a free massage machine available in the facility, and although small, there is a large public bath. The breakfast was quite luxurious, with a variety of selections, and it was very delicious. Additionally, there was a free drink offer of one cup per person per day, including alcoholic beverages. I would like to use it again.

name: HELIO HOSTEL SAPPORO
detail: I used it for a 2-night, 3-day stay due to some business. It was my first time using it, and overall it was clean and comfortable. Pros: - Cheap prices. - There is a café and lobby on the first floor where you can relax after checkout. - Amenities are well-stocked. - Conveniently located near a convenience store and Tanukikoji shopping street. - The staff are kind. - There is a women-only shower room. - It is quiet while sleeping. → I think it is perfectly comfortable for those who just want a place to sleep! Cons: - You can't eat food in the sleeping area, so you have to move to the space on the first or fifth floor (drinks are allowed). - It is quite difficult to place a suitcase on the upper bunk of the bunk bed (the ladder is attached and hard to climb). - The bed lighting uses an orange bulb, which made it personally difficult to apply makeup. The cons are minimal, and overall it was a hotel I would like to use again.

name: APA Hotel Sapporo Odori Ekimae Nishi
detail: I stayed at APA Hotel for the first time because it was affordable. From the moment I arrived, the staff were kind and attentive. The person who checked me in at the front desk was gentlemanly and helpful. I've stayed at various hotels, but this was the first time I received such considerate treatment, which left a strong impression on me. The room was efficient, and it was convenient to watch TV from the bed. It would be perfect if there were a large public bath. The bathroom was clean, and I felt it was just right for staying alone. They provided a room on a higher floor with a good view, for which I am grateful. The restaurant was also on-site, and the meals there were delicious! It was my first trip to Sapporo, and I checked out with a very good impression. I will definitely stay here again. I hope to get a room on a higher floor next time too... Thank you very much for your care.

name: Ten to Ten Hostel
detail: The facility was clean and comfortable to stay in. Although it was a dormitory type, each bed had partitions, which allowed me to relax without worrying about my surroundings, which I appreciated. It is a bit of a walk from the station, but it has good access to Hokkaido University, making it convenient as a base for sightseeing. On the other hand, there is no laundry facility in the building, so when I needed to do laundry, I had to walk about 15 minutes to a coin laundry. If you plan to stay multiple nights, I think it's good to take that into consideration. Overall, it was a clean and calming place to stay.

name: JR Inn Sapporo
detail: The location is great, just a 5-minute walk from Sapporo Station, and it's easy to find. The cleanliness of the accommodation, the attitude of the staff, soundproofing, water pressure, and facilities were all good. However, there is a subway track in front of the hotel, so it can be quite noisy and you can feel vibrations during operating hours. It might be difficult for light sleepers. The complimentary breakfast was also great, as they made sure nothing was missing.

name: Hotel Resol Sapporo Nakajima Koen
detail: Right behind Zepp Sapporo, I stayed after participating in the live event this time. I arrived early and parked at a nearby parking lot (the hotel has a multi-story parking lot as well) for only 1,100 yen for 24 hours, which is a bargain (≧∇≦*) The hotel is a bit old, but it is very well maintained and extremely comfortable✨️ The staff at the front desk are, of course, polite and have a good demeanor (≧∇≦*) The style of taking off shoes and relaxing in the room is nice because I can walk around barefoot without worry. While the windows are fixed (non-opening), the view of the TV tower from the large window gives a sense of openness. The facilities are honestly not the latest, but it doesn't bother me at all. There are small event services and a small, comfortable parfait offering! There are three convenience stores nearby, and the subway is close, making it easy to participate in any event venue (ﾉ*>∀<)ﾉ I can quickly reach Susukino and Odori as well (*•̀ㅂ•́)ו✧ I don't want to recommend it to anyone (¯−¯) Because I don't want it to be unavailable for me to stay in (*ˊ˘ˋ*) Keeping it a secret… is my true feeling, I guess Σ(｡>艸<｡)
